questions.q:
With reference to the functioning of Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. Article 85 requires that six months shall not intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.
2. The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution recommended at least 120 sitting days a year for the Lok Sabha.
3. Under Article 118, the rules of procedure of the Lok Sabha are made by the Speaker alone, without the House.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 118 lets each House make rules for its own procedure and conduct of business; it does not vest the power in the presiding officer alone. The magazine links the proposed rise in Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850 with the need for statutory minimum sittings, since Question Hour ran only 60% of scheduled time in the 17th Lok Sabha.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The 2008 delimitation redrew Lok Sabha constituency boundaries but did not change the number of seats allotted to any State.
Statement-II: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill proposes raising the strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. Seat allocation stayed unchanged in 2008 because the 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze, first imposed by the 42nd Amendment on the 1971 Census, until after the first Census published after 2026, while allowing boundaries to be redrawn on the 2001 Census.

questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's 2026 ruling in The Secretary to Government v. Sameer Ahamed N., consider the following statements:
1. It upheld the Madras High Court in striking down a Tamil Nadu order that let converts to Islam claim BC (Muslim) certificates on the basis of their pre-conversion caste.
2. It held that backwardness rooted in the Hindu caste order cannot simply be transposed into a non-Hindu social order.
3. It held that a Jamath may attest a conversion but cannot conclusively decide eligibility for BC status.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The Court reasoned that religion is not community: conversion gives religious affiliation, not membership of a community built on ancestry, endogamy and occupation. Grouping converts with no common characteristic violated Article 14, and a commission's advice could not save a classification failing Articles 14, 15(4) and 16(4). Reconversion needs a fact-specific inquiry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation for backward-class Muslims in Tamil Nadu:
1. The 3.5% quota for backward-class Muslims rests on a State Act of 2007.
2. Communities such as the Labbais, Mapilla and Dekkani Muslims are listed in the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The seven recognised communities (Ansar, Dekkani Muslims, Dudekula, Labbais including Rowthar and Marakayar, Mapilla, Sheik, Syed) are listed in section 3(a) of the Tamil Nadu reservation Act of 1993. Paragraph 3 of the 1950 Order confines Scheduled Caste status to persons professing Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism, so no Muslim group can appear in it.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Case : Point associated with it
1. G. Michael v. S. Venkateswaran : Claim of a Hindu-to-Christian convert to benefits linked to Scheduled Caste status
2. Kailash Sonkar v. Maya Devi : Approved the reasoning of the G. Michael case
3. Chinthada Anand v. Andhra Pradesh : Scheduled Caste status is 'eclipsed' on conversion to Christianity
4. Indra Sawhney v. Union of India : Examined the effect of change of religion on backwardness
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. In Sameer Ahamed the Court distinguished Indra Sawhney (1992) because it did not consider change of religion; it only recognised that social backwardness can exist in groups outside Hinduism. G. Michael (Madras HC, 1951) was approved in Kailash Sonkar (1983) and C. Selvarani (2024); Chinthada Anand is a 2026 ruling.

questions.q:
With reference to preventive detention in India, consider the following statements:
1. Entry 9 of the Union List covers preventive detention for reasons connected with defence, foreign affairs or the security of India.
2. Entry 3 of the Concurrent List covers preventive detention for reasons connected with the security of a State, public order or essential supplies and services.
3. MISA, heavily used during the Emergency, was repealed in 1978.
4. Under Article 22(4), detention beyond three months generally requires review by an Advisory Board.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The laws in force are the National Security Act, 1980 and COFEPOSA, 1974; the Preventive Detention Act, 1950 lapsed in 1969. Article 22(5) adds that grounds must be communicated as soon as possible with a chance to make a representation. The Supreme Court revisited these safeguards during the October 2026 anti-CEC protests in Delhi.

questions.q:
With reference to Mulla Afroz v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2026), consider the following statements:
1. Section 23 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 bars proving against an accused a confession made to a police officer, except one made in the immediate presence of a Magistrate or the part that leads to discovery of a fact.
2. The Court held that using the same incident and material as the criminal case to keep a person in jail after bail makes the detention punitive rather than preventive.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Court quashed an NSA detention resting on a police confession: material inadmissible to prove guilt cannot by itself found the 'subjective satisfaction' for detention, which remains reviewable. It also rejected grounds such as CCTV footage never supplied to the detenu and a charge sheet, which is only the agency's opinion, under Article 22(5).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita is not a form of preventive detention.
Statement-II: Section 163 orders regulate activities and assemblies, whereas preventive detention holds an individual under a specific law.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Section 163 (successor to Section 144 CrPC) lets an Executive Magistrate issue urgent written orders against nuisance or apprehended danger; such orders need urgency and sufficient grounds and are open to judicial review. Detention of individuals needs a law such as the NSA, 1980 with Article 22 safeguards.

questions.q: An order made by an Executive Magistrate under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ordinarily remains in force for not more than
questions.e: Section 163 orders lapse in two months, as under the old Section 144 CrPC. Babulal Parate (1961) upheld the power but said it is not unlimited; the Ramlila Maidan case (2012) confined it to grave, sudden emergencies. A 2023 RTI study of about 5,400 Delhi orders found only 1.5% restricted unlawful assemblies.

questions.q:
With reference to security proceedings ('peace bonds') under Chapter IX of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, consider the following statements:
1. They are directed against identified persons and require a written show-cause order and an inquiry.
2. The amount of the bond must be deposited in cash when the bond is executed.
3. The procedure was retained even though the Second Administrative Reforms Commission recommended its repeal.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Bond money is paid only on forfeiture (Section 491). The procedure was retained on the advice of the Law Commission (1969) and the 2nd ARC (2007), and was upheld in Madhu Limaye (1970). An inquiry lapses after six months; default can mean jail up to one year (Sections 126-128) or three years (Section 129).

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs in the context of the electoral-roll controversy of 2026:
Item : Description
1. Annexure-D : Declaration added to Form 7 asking applicants to align birth dates with Citizenship Act provisions and give lineage documents
2. Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 : Rule-making power vested in the Election Commission
3. Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 : Punishment for false declarations
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 3 is correct. Annexure-D was added to Form 6, the enrolment form, during the SIR. Section 28 vests rule-making power in the Central Government, so critics argued the ECI could not alter a statutory form alone or run different Form 6 versions in SIR and non-SIR States, drawing the charge of a 'back-door NRC' and questions under Articles 14 and 326.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a Special Summary Revision, existing electors are carried into the draft roll automatically.
2. The expression 'Special Intensive Revision' is used in Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Section 21(3) only lets the ECI order a 'special revision'; Rule 25 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 recognises intensive and summary revisions. 'Special Intensive Revision' appears nowhere in the statute, which raised the question whether Article 324 can support a procedure beyond the law. In an SIR voters must submit an enumeration form.

questions.q:
With reference to the Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls announced on 15 October 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It covers 17 States and Union Territories, including Assam, where no Special Intensive Revision was held.
2. Its qualifying date is 1 January 2027.
3. Under a 2022 amendment, any elector of the constituency, and not only of the same booth, may file a Form 7 objection.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The 17 (14 States and 3 UTs) are mainly those where the SIR was completed in 2025-26, plus Assam; the draft roll was due on 12 November 2026 and the final roll on 4 January 2027. The 2022 Form 7 change is the root of fears of bulk objections, reported from Uttarakhand and Karnataka.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events relating to the Election Commission of India in chronological order:
1. Supreme Court's Constitution Bench judgment in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India
2. Appointment of S.S. Dhanoa and V.S. Seigell as Election Commissioners
3. CEC N. Gopalaswami's recommendation to remove Election Commissioner Navin Chawla
4. Appointment of M.S. Gill and G.V.G. Krishnamurthy as Election Commissioners
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Dhanoa and Seigell were appointed in October 1989 and removed by the next government; Gill and Krishnamurthy came in October 1993 through an ordinance; Seshan (1995) held that all three Commissioners are equal and decide by majority; Gopalaswami's suo motu recommendation of January 2009 was rejected because the CEC cannot act under Article 324(5) without a reference.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In 2009, CEC N. Gopalaswami's recommendation to remove Election Commissioner Navin Chawla was not acted upon by the President.
Statement-II: Under Article 324(5), the CEC may recommend the removal of an Election Commissioner on his own initiative, and the President is bound by that recommendation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect. President Pratibha Patil rejected the suo motu recommendation because the CEC cannot act under Article 324(5) without a proper reference. The episode is part of the story of the multi-member Commission, from the 1989 appointments through the 1993 ordinance to Seshan (1995), behind October's objections by two Commissioners.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Entry in the Seventh Schedule : Subject
1. List I, Entry 54 : Regulation of mines and mineral development under Union control in the public interest
2. List II, Entry 23 : Regulation of mines and mineral development, subject to Union law
3. List II, Entry 50 : Taxes on mineral rights, subject to limitations imposed by Parliament
4. List II, Entry 49 : Royalty on minerals extracted
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Entry 49 of the State List covers taxes on lands and buildings, which the 2024 judgment held includes mineral-bearing land. The MMDR Amendment Act, 2026 restricts States from taxing mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands except as the Union permits, and invalidates certain uncollected pre-amendment taxes.

questions.q:
With reference to Mineral Area Development Authority v. Steel Authority of India Ltd. (2024), consider the following statements:
1. The MMDR Act, 1957, as it then stood, already restricted State taxation of mineral rights.
2. Parliament may by law limit, and even prohibit, State taxes on mineral rights.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Court found that the 1957 Act contained no such restriction, and that Entry 54 of the Union List alone cannot curtail State taxes on mineral-bearing land under Entry 49. The MMDR Amendment Act, 2026 is in effect Parliament now enacting such limits, which Karnataka, Telangana, Himachal Pradesh and Kerala plan to challenge.

questions.q: According to CAG data for 2024-25 cited in the debate on the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, mineral receipts formed the largest share of non-tax revenue in which one of the following States?
questions.e: Jharkhand's mineral receipts were about 85% of its non-tax revenue and Odisha's about 80% (the text rounds both to 'around 80%'). Karnataka was 48%, while Chhattisgarh was only 6%. Jharkhand warned its social-security programmes may suffer; Odisha's response was mixed, and MP, Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh have not challenged the Act.

questions.q:
With reference to the right to protest in Delhi, consider the following statements:
1. Article 19(3) permits restrictions on peaceful assembly in the interests of decency or morality.
2. Article 239AA(3)(a) brings police and public order within the legislative power of the Delhi Legislative Assembly.
3. The de-notification of Jantar Mantar on 12 October 2026 banned protests throughout Delhi.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Article 19(3) allows restrictions on assembly only for the sovereignty and integrity of India and public order. Article 239AA(3)(a) excludes State List Entries 1, 2 and 18 (public order, police, land) from the Delhi Assembly; Delhi Police works under the MHA. De-notification moved protests to Ramlila, Burari and CBD Grounds rather than banning them.

questions.q: In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar (1966), the Supreme Court described three concentric circles. Which one of the following represents the smallest and gravest circle?
questions.e: Law and order is the largest circle (local disturbances), public order lies within it (disturbance to the community at large) and security of the State is the smallest and gravest. So not every breach of the peace threatens public order, a distinction relevant when Delhi Police shifted protest sites amid the anti-CEC agitation.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Case : Holding
1. Himat Lal K. Shah (1972) : Police may require prior permission for street meetings but cannot ban assemblies on every street
2. Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan v. Union of India (2018) : Protests near Jantar Mantar must be regulated, not prohibited altogether
3. Mathuri v. State of Punjab (1963) : Knowing that entry would annoy is not the same as an intent to annoy
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. MKSS allowed areas to be earmarked and kept a limited part of Jantar Mantar Road for small regulated protests. Mathuri was cited when Cockroach Janta Party leaders were sent to judicial custody for entering the de-notified site; the Kerala HC has also held trespass is against possession, not ownership.

questions.q:
With reference to legislative privilege, consider the following statements:
1. In the Searchlight case (1959), the Supreme Court held that privileges under Article 194(3) can include the power to prohibit publication of proceedings.
2. The Keshav Singh opinion was given under the Supreme Court's advisory jurisdiction.
3. Sita Soren v. Union of India (2024) overruled P.V. Narasimha Rao on immunity for bribery linked to speeches or votes.
4. In October 2026 a seven-judge Bench in N. Ravi v. Speaker laid down that Article 19(1)(a) prevails over legislative privilege.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Bench under CJI Surya Kant disposed of the N. Ravi reference as infructuous, because the Tamil Nadu Assembly had withdrawn its 2003 resolution in 2004, keeping the questions open. Keshav Singh was an Article 143 reference (Shankar dates it 1964, the Recitals 1965) holding privileges are not absolute.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution protects the publication in a newspaper of a substantially true report of proceedings of Parliament or a State Legislature, subject to conditions?
questions.e: Article 361A protects substantially true reports of legislative proceedings unless malicious. Articles 105 and 194 deal with the powers and privileges of Parliament and State legislatures, and 194(3) leaves them to be defined by law. The NCRWC recommended codifying privileges; the N. Ravi reference closed without settling their reach against the press.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding sentencing reform:
1. In Sunita Devi v. State of Bihar (2024), the Supreme Court asked the Centre to consider a national sentencing policy.
2. The Sentencing Council of England and Wales was created under the Coroners and Justice Act, 2009.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Court said sentencing should not be a 'mere lottery', and the Centre has asked the Law Commission to examine a Sentencing Council. The BNS, 2023 fixes maximum and minimum sentences but lists no aggravating or mitigating factors; a Council would set starting points and ranges, with judges giving reasons for departures.

questions.q:
With reference to sentencing law in India, consider the following statements:
1. Section 258(2) of the BNSS provides for a separate hearing on sentence after conviction by a Court of Session.
2. Both criminal law and prisons are subjects in the Concurrent List.
3. The Probation of Offenders Act was enacted in 1978.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Criminal law is in the Concurrent List but prisons are in the State List, one reason for federal variation in sentencing outcomes. The Probation of Offenders Act dates from 1958; BNSS Sections 401-402 also allow release on probation or after admonition. Pendency had crossed 5.90 crore cases on the NJDG in October 2026.

questions.q:
With reference to the debate over Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's public remarks, consider the following statements:
1. The Restatement of Values of Judicial Life was adopted by Parliament through a resolution in 1997.
2. Principle 4.11 of the Bangalore Principles of Judicial Conduct allows judges to write, lecture and teach on law.
3. In ADR v. ECI (2026), the Supreme Court struck down the Bihar SIR.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Restatement was adopted by the Supreme Court's Full Court on 7 May 1997; its Clause 8 bars public views on matters pending or likely to arise. ADR v. ECI upheld the Bihar SIR, holding the right to vote neither absolute nor unregulated, with Rule 21A requiring notice, inquiry and a reasoned order before deletion.

questions.q:
With reference to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It removed the provision recognising self-perceived gender identity.
2. It lets a person obtain an identity certificate from the District Magistrate on self-declaration alone, without any medical board.
3. It gives effect to the NALSA (2014) principle that medical certification is the basis of gender recognition.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The amendment requires a medical board's recommendation before the DM issues a certificate and makes a revised certificate mandatory after specified surgery. NALSA (2014) recognised self-identified gender, the opposite of medical certification. The Act received assent on 30 March 2026 and came into force on 25 May 2026; a PIL seeks to keep women-specific protections for biological females.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in the context of deploying private employees as Census enumerators:
1. Since Article 23(2) is self-executing, no statute is needed to compel private employees to do Census work.
2. The National Service Act, 1972 provides for compulsory service by specified categories such as doctors and engineers, with safeguards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Article 23(2) permits compulsory service for public purposes, but a statute must authorise it; the open question is whether Section 4(2) of the Census Act, 1948 covers private employees, given its narrower Sections 6-7. Courts quashed LIC deployments in 2010 and 2019, and Dulal Samanta (1958) upheld compulsory special police officers.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Provision : Content
1. Section 4(2), Census Act, 1948 : State governments may appoint persons as Census officers, who are bound to serve
2. Section 4A, Census Act, 1948 : Private establishments must provide staff for general Census deployment
3. Section 15, Census Act, 1948 : Individual records are confidential and inadmissible in civil proceedings
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Section 4A obliges local authorities to provide staff when directed; Sections 6-7 deal with private establishments, mainly for counting people in their charge. Census is in Entry 69 of the Union List. About 31 lakh staff are being trained for Census 2027, the 16th Census and 8th since Independence.

questions.q:
With reference to the dispute over senior posts in the Central Armed Police Forces, consider the following statements:
1. The contempt petitions and the challenge to the CAPF (General Administration) Act, 2026 are being heard by different Benches.
2. Officers recruited directly into the CAPF cadre join as Deputy Commandants.
3. The Supreme Court allowed the Centre's review petition against its May 2025 judgment.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The contempt pleas and the challenge to the Act are before the same Bench. Cadre officers enter as Assistant Commandants. The Centre's review petition was dismissed in October 2025; the May 2025 judgment had ordered a progressive cut in IPS deputation up to SAG level within two years, while the Act overrides court decrees through a non-obstante clause.

questions.q:
With reference to reservation for Backward Classes in local bodies, consider the following statements:
1. Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6) enable reservation for Backward Classes but fix neither its basis nor its quantum.
2. The 'triple test' was made mandatory in Vikas Kishan Rao Gawali v. State of Maharashtra (2021).
3. Quotas for women are vertical and must fit, along with SC, ST and BC quotas, within the 50% ceiling.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Women's quotas are horizontal and cut across the vertical SC, ST and BC quotas. The Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down orders raising BC reservation to 34% in rural and 33.33% in urban bodies because the State relied on a general household survey, not a local-body-wise study of political backwardness; the SC dismissed the appeal.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a component of the 'triple test' for reservation of Backward Classes in local bodies?
o: Use of caste data from the decennial Census released by the Registrar General
Specification of the proportion of reservation local-body-wise in the light of the commission's findings
Keeping combined SC, ST and Backward Class reservation within 50%
A dedicated commission to conduct an empirical inquiry into the political backwardness of Backward Classes
questions.e: The triple test from Gawali (2021) needs a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportions set by it, and a combined ceiling of 50%; Census caste data is not one of its elements. Suresh Mahajan (2022) held that seats go to the General category where the test is not met. AP's combined reservation had reached 61.08% in rural bodies.

questions.q:
With reference to Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish (2026), consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court held that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a), held by children irrespective of age.
2. The Court endorsed a blanket ban on social media for children below 16 years.
3. Platforms must acknowledge complaints about child sexual exploitation and abuse material within two hours.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Court called blanket curbs 'unproven measures of proven disproportionality' while allowing parental oversight and a 'child mode'. Platforms must report CSEAM removals within 2 hours and acknowledge complaints within 24 hours, using a National Hash and URL List Database; the Union must amend the IT Rules, 2021 before the 10 December 2026 hearing.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020), the Supreme Court declared access to the internet itself a fundamental right.
Statement-II: In the same case, the Court held that internet shutdowns must meet the test of proportionality.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct. Bhasin protected speech and trade carried on online and required proportionate shutdowns, but stopped short of declaring internet access a right; the 2026 Just Rights for Children Alliance ruling settled that. Cricket Association of Bengal (1995) had earlier read the right to receive and impart information into Article 19(1)(a).

questions.q:
With reference to Overseas Citizens of India (OCI), consider the following statements:
1. The OCI scheme was introduced in 2005.
2. Section 7B of the Citizenship Act bars OCI cardholders from voting or contesting elections.
3. Cancellation of OCI registration under Section 7D requires that the cardholder be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
4. A 'Leave India' direction under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 likewise requires a prior hearing.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The 2025 Act treats OCIs as foreigners; Section 7(2)(c) lets the government bar a foreigner from staying and powers are delegated to FRROs, with no hearing required. This asymmetry surfaced when actor Imran Khan, a US citizen, was told to leave after an anti-CEC protest; the Bombay HC stayed the notice.

questions.q: In Louis De Raedt v. Union of India (1991), the Supreme Court held that a foreigner in India is entitled to which one of the following?
o: The right to reside and settle in any part of India
The right to freedom of peaceful assembly
The right to move freely throughout India
The protection of life and personal liberty under Article 21
questions.e: Foreigners enjoy Article 21, but Article 19 freedoms, including 19(1)(e) on residing and settling, are for citizens only. Hans Muller of Nurenburg (1955) upheld wide expulsion powers under the Foreigners Act, 1946. In October the Delhi HC held a valid visa gives no enforceable right to enter, and Section 3 of the 2025 Act allows refusal on security grounds.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding casteist abuse on social media:
1. In Sri Sayan Mondal v. State of West Bengal, the Calcutta High Court held that 'within public view' under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 can extend to the digital domain.
2. In Hitesh Verma v. State of Uttarakhand (2020), the Supreme Court held that an insult in a private enclosed space generally does not satisfy the 'public view' requirement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Calcutta HC applied Sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) to a Facebook post and directed police to use cyber-forensic and IP-log tracing before saying an accused cannot be traced. The ingredients remain an accused who is not SC/ST, an intentional caste-based insult and public view, each judged on its own facts.

questions.q:
With reference to the National Tribunals Commission set up under the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It consists of a Chairperson, who is a retired Supreme Court judge or a retired High Court Chief Justice, and four members, two judicial and two technical.
2. Articles 323A and 323B, under which tribunals are created, were inserted by the 42nd Amendment.
3. Recruitment is to begin at least six months before a vacancy arises, through Search-cum-Selection Committees.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The NTC, headquartered in New Delhi, will appoint heads and members of 16 tribunals and appellate bodies, with interviews and order-writing tests, formal misconduct inquiries and a National Tribunals Data Grid. Critics warn of residual executive influence and that procedure alone cannot fix pendency, so they seek judicial participation and financial autonomy.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not among the directions on appointment of Directors General of Police laid down in Prakash Singh v. Union of India (2006)?
o: The DGP is chosen from a panel of three senior IPS officers prepared by the UPSC
An officer needs at least six months of residual service to be considered
The DGP gets a minimum tenure of two years
The panel is prepared by the State Public Service Commission after an interview
questions.e: The panel is prepared by the UPSC, to which States must send records at least three months before the vacancy. The Supreme Court is examining Jharkhand's 2025 DGP Regulation, challenged by the Union, and has asked amicus Raju Ramachandran with the UPSC to review all States' police laws and DGP appointments.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding compensation for railway passengers:
1. The Optional Travel Insurance Scheme has applied to counter tickets since its launch.
2. Sections 124 and 124A of the Railways Act, 1989 provide no-fault compensation for accidents and untoward incidents, decided by the Railway Claims Tribunal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. OTIS covered only online (IRCTC) confirmed or RAC tickets, at 45 paise per passenger per journey with cover of Rs 10 lakh for death. The Supreme Court directed the same insurance on counter tickets from 27 October 2026. Critics note that insurance is not safety and urge Kavach, fencing and foot overbridges.

questions.q:
With reference to scholarships for Scheduled Caste students, consider the following statements:
1. The Pre- and Post-Matric Scholarship schemes are fully funded by the Centre.
2. Component 2 of the Pre-Matric Scholarship, for children of parents in unclean or hazardous occupations, is open to any caste or religion with no income ceiling.
3. The Post-Matric Scholarship has no family-income ceiling.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The schemes are Centrally Sponsored, run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, with 60:40 sharing (90:10 in the North-East). The Post-Matric income ceiling is Rs 2.5 lakh. The PAC questioned 'fraud markers' flagged by the CAG; in 2025-26 Post-Matric reached 36.07 lakh students against a target of 76.55 lakh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding judicial intervention in local-body elections:
1. Article 243ZG allows courts to question the delimitation of municipal wards through a writ petition at any stage.
2. In N.P. Ponnuswami (1952), the Supreme Court held that courts may freely interfere once the election process has begun.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Article 243ZG bars courts from interfering in delimitation and seat allotment, with challenges only by election petition, and Ponnuswami read Article 329(b) as barring interference once the process starts. Yet in YSRCP v. State of AP (2026) the SC held that free nominations are part of free and fair elections and asked the SEC to consider extending the deadline.

questions.q: The Press Council of India, which issued guidelines for journalists covering protests in October 2026, is a statutory body constituted under the
o: Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867
Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023
questions.e: The PCI is a statutory quasi-judicial body under the Press Council Act, 1978. Its guidelines ask reporters to carry a press card or PIB/DIP accreditation, stay neutral, follow lawful police instructions and avoid broadcasting real-time police positions. Critics say they are advisory, one-sided and leave freelance and digital reporters without accreditation.

questions.q:
With reference to the constitutional scheme for elections, consider the following statements:
1. Article 325 permits separate electoral rolls for different religious communities.
2. Article 326 fixes the voting age at 21 years.
3. Article 324 vests superintendence of Panchayat elections in the Election Commission of India.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Article 325 provides one general roll per constituency with no exclusion on religion, race, caste or sex; Article 326 provides adult suffrage, with the age now 18 after the 61st Amendment (static GK). Article 324 covers Parliament, State legislatures, President and Vice-President; Panchayat polls are run by State Election Commissions under Article 243K.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Research has conclusively shown that screen time directly causes harmful structural changes in children's brains.
Statement-II: The prefrontal cortex, which governs attention, memory and decisions, continues to mature into early adulthood.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct. The magazine notes that research has not conclusively shown that screen time causes harmful brain change; effects depend on duration, content and context. Short videos, autoplay and notifications hurt sustained attention, and over-reliance on AI can weaken reasoning, so it urges evidence-based and child-centred design.
